findings.title: track_visit! uses the topic id as the user id for non-User arguments
findings.body: `TopicUser.track_visit!(topic, user)` sets `user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic`. `TopicsController#track_visit_to_topic` calls this with a topic id and a user id, so the second argument is an Integer and the false branch assigns the topic id to `user_id`. This updates or creates `topic_users` rows for the wrong user, corrupting visit tracking and potentially causing foreign-key errors. The else branch should return `user`.

findings.title: Unsubscribe action assumes a TopicUser row exists
findings.body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` looks up `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and immediately reads `tu.notification_level`. A logged-in user can request this route for a topic where no `topic_users` row exists yet, so `tu` is nil and the action raises `NoMethodError`, producing a 500. Use `TopicUser.change` or find-or-create the record before mutating it.

findings.title: Notification level change bypasses TopicUser.change side effects
findings.body: The unsubscribe action mutates `notification_level` and calls `save!` directly. `TopicUser.change` is the normal API for this operation and also sets `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id`, publishes the MessageBus notification-level change, and runs observer callbacks. Bypassing it can leave client state stale and make notification-level changes inconsistently recorded.

findings.title: GET unsubscribe immediately mutates notification settings
findings.body: The route maps GET `/t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` to an action that changes the user's topic notification level before rendering anything. Because the mutation happens on a GET, link prefetching, email-client scanners, previews, or repeated reloads can change a logged-in user's notification state without an explicit confirmation. A state-changing unsubscribe should require POST/PUT or an explicit user action.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for all callers
findings.body: `MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` append `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, but the updated locale string interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`; any other Discourse or plugin caller enabling `add_unsubscribe_link` without that key may get a missing-interpolation error or broken email text, and non-topic emails will incorrectly refer to a particular topic.

findings.title: Missing tests for the new unsubscribe behavior
findings.body: The spec only adds `unsubscribe_url` to the builder but does not assert that the body or HTML part includes the topic unsubscribe link. There are also no controller/request specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` covering missing `TopicUser` rows, slug redirects, permissions, or the GET mutation, which are the main failure modes introduced by this PR.
